questions.prompt: An analyst proposes rebooting AHU-OT1 during surgery to fix a weak configuration. What should determine the work window?

options.text: The analyst's next available hour
The shortest contractor visit, even if surgery is underway
A slot agreed with the theatre team when no patient depends on the system
The date on the security ticket alone

questions.explanation: Clinical safety determines timing. The chapter tells the analyst to ask the theatre manager when lists run and schedule work when no patient depends on the air-handling system.

questions.prompt: Why can postponing a security change by a few days be the safer choice in this chapter's theatre example?

options.text: The security risk disappears automatically after a few days
The delay can secure a clinical work window instead of interrupting surgery
Only contractors may decide whether patients are at risk
The AHU never affects a theatre's conditions

questions.explanation: A short delay to reach an agreed safe slot is normally acceptable; rushing a change during surgery can harm patients and is explicitly rejected in §2.1.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of building system and fallback matches the contingency examples in the chapter?

options.text: Piped oxygen supply — cylinder oxygen
Piped oxygen supply — manual door keys
Door access control — portable cooling
HVAC or chillers — elevator rescue procedure

questions.explanation: The contingency examples pair cylinder oxygen with failed piped supply, manual keys with doors, and portable cooling with HVAC or chillers.

questions.prompt: A plan lists cylinder oxygen, but no one has checked the supply or knows who starts it at night. How should security treat that plan?

options.text: As a proven fallback because it appears in an inventory
As authorization to isolate the gas system immediately
As evidence that a cyber incident has already occurred
As an unverified fallback that must be checked with estates before relying on it

questions.explanation: The chapter says a cylinder supply nobody has checked is not a usable fallback. Security should ask when it was exercised and who starts it at night.

questions.prompt: At Millbrook, who controls work on the medical-gas systems?

options.text: The IT security analyst acting alone
The medical-gas authorised person under the relevant estates process
Any contractor who has physical access
The lift-rescue team

questions.explanation: The chapter assigns medical-gas control to the authorised person; estates authorises building work, while IT security advises rather than directs gas changes.

questions.prompt: Aisha finds a weak controller password. Which path respects the authority described in the chapter?

options.text: Tell the contractor directly to change it without a permit
Change it herself while the theatre is operating
Report it to the estates manager, who arranges an authorised contractor change under a permit
Publish the password so clinicians can decide whether to change it

questions.explanation: Aisha reports the weakness to the estates manager. The manager arranges contractor work under a permit, preserving patient-safety checks and an approval record.

questions.prompt: Why might opening a ceiling panel for a firmware-label check in a theatre require infection-control approval?

options.text: It can release dust into a clinical area
It automatically changes the controller firmware
It replaces the theatre manager's scheduling authority
It proves that the air system is compromised

questions.explanation: The chapter identifies dust released by opening ceiling panels in a theatre as a reason for infection-control approval in addition to an estates permit.

questions.prompt: In the synthetic Saturday firmware-label visit, what closes the authorised work record correctly?

options.text: Leave the permit open because no settings changed
Close the permit when the work ends, recording approvals even though settings were untouched
Ask the analyst to sign for the contractor after surgery
Delete the photographs because the work was non-invasive

questions.explanation: The example records the estates permit, theatre confirmation and contractor escort; the permit is closed at 07:40 despite no settings being touched.

questions.prompt: Which request to clinicians best follows the chapter's communication guidance?

options.text: Approve our protocol list without asking about patient risk
We will change theatre air controls at an unspecified time
IT security has sole authority over theatre scheduling
We need one agreed hour to check this theatre system; here is the patient risk and how we will verify the work

questions.explanation: The chapter recommends a short, concrete request explaining which theatre, which hour, what will happen, patient risk and how the work will be checked.

questions.prompt: Why does documenting manual or alternate support help when suggesting BMS isolation during an incident?

options.text: It proves all building equipment can remain off indefinitely
It eliminates the need for estates and clinical approval
It shows how patients can remain supported while an untrusted networked system is isolated
It turns an untested contingency list into a tested plan

questions.explanation: Known, verified fallback arrangements allow security staff to propose isolation while explaining how patients stay supported; they do not remove approval or testing needs.
